title: Coroner still awaiting autopsy results for Sidney man who died in custody
article: The B.C. Coroner's Service has yet to determine how a 32-year- old Sidney man died after being arrested by Sidney RCMP last November.
Coroner Maureen Wint said Wednesday that she is still awaiting a final autopsy report on the death of Lyndon Charles Valan.
As with any in-custody death, the case will be the subject of a coroner's inquest.

Valan died after he was arrested at a residence on Melville Drive. An RCMP spokesman said at the time that police had received two 911 calls from the residence Nov. 29, 2003, and initially focused on getting Valan's mother and a teenage girl out of the house.
RCMP said that Valan appeared to be under the influence of drugs and confronted officers outside the house with a kitchen knife and a large boxcutter.
He dropped the weapons when ordered to by police, but became violent again after he was placed in handcuffs, police said.
Valan went into cardiac arrest in an ambulance on the way to the Saanich Peninsula Hospital. He died later in emergency.
It was the latest in a series of tragic incidents to beset the Valan family over the years.

In 1997, Valan's sister, Lavinia, was killed on the Patricia Bay Highway when a Geo Metro ran a red light and collided with a van. Lavinia Valan, who was in the back seat of the Metro, was thrown from the car and died from massive head injuries. The 24-year-old driver later pleaded guilty to dangerous driving causing death. He received an 18-month jail term.
Three years earlier, another sister, Laurel Valan, died in Duncan when her Dodge pickup truck failed to negotiate a corner, struck a power pole and rolled, RCMP said.
Lyndon Valan's obituary stated that he is survived by his mother, Dorothy, father, son Chavez, three brothers and five sisters.
